costDefaults.label: Retail, towels & member supplies
costDefaults.sourceNote: Shaker bottles, drinks, towel service and cleaning consumables that scale with the member count rather than the building.

costDefaults.label: Front desk & floor trainers
costDefaults.sourceNote: One block ≈ 1.4 FTEs of desk and floor coverage at $15/hr per 400 members; coverage hours scale with the membership that shows up.

costDefaults.label: General manager
costDefaults.sourceNote: Salaried GM at $52k/yr; sells memberships and runs the floor regardless of the count.

costDefaults.label: Rent

benchmarkBand.source: IHRSA industry data — quarterly rent for 6,000-12,000 sq ft of big-box or second-generation retail

costDefaults.sourceNote: 8,000 sq ft at $20/sq ft/yr NNN. A gym is a real-estate business with dumbbells: the square footage IS the product — and every extra foot is rent the members pay for through the ramp years.

laborPctOfRevenue.source: IHRSA industry data — membership gyms without large PT books; studios with instructor-led classes run far higher

occupancyPctOfRevenue.source: IHRSA industry data — full OCCUPANCY line; gyms are the most occupancy-heavy business in this catalog by design

ebitdaMarginPct.source: IHRSA industry data — independent mid-market clubs at stabilized membership; note EBITDA flatters a gym, whose equipment wears out fast
